recipes.title: Scrambled eggs
recipes.summary: Soft eggs for four, ready in about 8 minutes. Keep the heat low, and take them off while they still look a little glossy.
recipes.style: Skillet, about 8 minutes. Low-carb as written.

photo.caption: Photograph by OmegaFallon, CC BY 4.0. It shows scrambled eggs with basil. This recipe uses optional chives or cheddar, not basil.
photo.author: OmegaFallon
photo.changes: Saved a JPEG whose longest side is 1600 pixels.

steps.text: Crack the eggs into a bowl. Add the cream, if you are using it, and a pinch of salt. Whisk until you see no streaks of white.
Melt the butter in a 10 to 12 inch nonstick pan over medium-low heat.
Pour in the eggs. Wait about 20 seconds, until the edges just begin to set.

timers.label: Edges start to set
timers.note: Then start pushing the eggs into large soft curds.

steps.text: Push slowly with a silicone spatula from the edges toward the center, making large soft curds. Stir every few seconds. When the eggs are mostly set but still a little glossy and wet-looking, take the pan off the heat. They keep cooking in the hot pan.
Fold in the cheese if you are using it. Season with pepper and serve right away.

tips.title: Tips
items: Low and slow beats high heat. High heat makes them rubbery and dry.
Pull them off while they are still slightly underdone. They keep cooking in the hot pan.
Use a nonstick pan and a silicone spatula.
Don't salt the eggs and then let them sit. Salting right before cooking is fine.
For 8 or more eggs, use the bigger pan, or cook two batches.
If you are cooking bacon too, eggs go in the pan last so they are hot.

tasks.label: Crack 8 eggs into a bowl

recipes.title: Fried eggs
recipes.summary: Sunny-side up, over easy, over medium, or over hard. About 5 minutes, and 1 to 4 eggs per batch.
recipes.servingsNote: Written for 2 adults, 2 eggs each. The portion control opens at 3 adults and scales from 2. A 10 inch pan fits 2 or 3 eggs at a time.
recipes.style: Skillet, about 5 minutes. Low-carb as written.
recipes.authoring: Household plan for weekday breakfast. Newly written as a standing card, not a dinner on the week.

photo.alt: Two sunny-side up eggs with black pepper cooking in a black pan.
photo.caption: Photograph by Balise42, CC BY-SA 4.0. It shows two sunny-side up eggs in a pan. This recipe also covers over easy, over medium, and over hard.
photo.author: Balise42
photo.changes: Saved a JPEG whose longest side is 1280 pixels.

ingredients.name: large eggs
ingredients.note: 2 per adult. Cook 1 to 4 per batch

steps.text: Heat a nonstick pan over medium-low for about 1 minute. Add the butter and let it melt and foam. If the butter browns quickly, the heat is too high, so turn it down.

timers.label: Warm the pan
timers.note: Then add the butter. If it browns quickly, turn the heat down.

steps.text: Crack each egg into a small bowl or cup first. Then gently slide it into the pan from close to the surface.
Leave the eggs alone. Do not poke, stir, or move them. Give them 2 to 3 minutes, until the whites are fully set and opaque.

timers.label: Whites set
timers.note: Start with 2 minutes. They may need 3, until the whites are fully set and opaque.

steps.text: Sunny-side up: cover the pan with a lid for the last 30 to 60 seconds to set the top of the whites, then slide the eggs out.

timers.label: Sunny-side lid
timers.note: 30 to 60 seconds, just long enough to set the top of the whites.

steps.text: Over easy, over medium, or over hard: once the whites are mostly set, slide a thin wide spatula fully under one egg in one confident motion. Flip gently, close to the pan. Cook 15 to 30 seconds for over easy, about 1 minute for over medium, or 2 minutes for over hard. Then flip the egg back or slide it out.

timers.label: Over easy
timers.note: 15 to 30 seconds for a runny yolk.

timers.label: Over medium
timers.note: About 1 minute.

timers.label: Over hard
timers.note: About 2 minutes.

tips.title: Why my fried eggs fall apart (and how to fix it)
items: Don't crack an egg straight into the pan. Crack it into a cup first, so shell bits and a broken yolk stay out, and so you can lower it in gently.
Fresh eggs hold together better. Older eggs have runny whites that spread out.
Use medium-low heat, not high, so the bottom does not stick and crisp before the top sets.
Use plenty of fat and a good nonstick pan.
Give each egg room. Don't crowd the pan. Two or three eggs fit in a 10 inch pan.
Don't touch an egg until the white is set. Moving it early breaks it apart.
Use a thin, wide spatula, such as a fish spatula or a thin silicone turner. Get it all the way under the egg before you lift.
Flip low and gentle, close to the pan. A high toss is what breaks the yolk.
If a yolk breaks, call it over hard. It is still tasty.
Wiggle the pan. If the egg slides freely, it is ready to flip.
The lid trick sets the top of the whites, so you can skip flipping entirely.

tasks.label: Set a nonstick pan on medium-low
Have a thin wide spatula ready
